◦ Emotional appeal — *"messages that provoke anger or fear are forwarded far more readily than sober corrections."*
◦ Trust in the sender — *"Many people share a message simply because it came from a trusted friend or relative."*

 

• The remedy is given in the third paragraph — readers should verify a startling claim against an established news organisation, examine the date and source of a photograph, and treat any message demanding immediate circulation with suspicion.

 

• The closing sentence sums up both halves: *"Technology created this problem, but the habits of ordinary readers will determine how far it spreads."*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 is contradicted twice over — the passage expressly says the reasons have "little to do with technology alone", and it nowhere mentions stricter laws.

 

• Option 2 reverses the passage, which treats established news organisations as the standard against which claims should be checked.

 

• Option 3 misuses a detail. Schools are mentioned only as an encouraging development, not as the cause of the problem.

 

NOTE

 

• For two-part questions of this kind, verify both halves of the option before choosing it. A distractor is often built by pairing one correct element with one false one.

question: Which ruler founded the Chalukya dynasty of Vatapi (Badami)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pulakeshin I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pulakeshin I founded the Chalukya dynasty of Vatapi, the modern Badami in the Bagalkot district of Karnataka, in about 543 CE. (वातापी के चालुक्य — संस्थापक पुलकेशिन प्रथम)

 

• He fortified the hill at Vatapi and performed the Ashvamedha sacrifice to proclaim his sovereignty. The dynasty is also known as the Badami Chalukyas or Early Western Chalukyas.

 

• The greatest ruler of the line was Pulakeshin II (609-642 CE), who defeated Harshavardhana on the banks of the Narmada — an event recorded in the Aihole inscription, composed by his court poet Ravikirti. The Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang visited his kingdom. He was ultimately defeated and killed by the Pallava ruler Narasimhavarman I, who captured Badami in 642 CE.

 

• The Chalukyas were great builders. The temples at Badami, Aihole and Pattadakal belong to their period; Aihole is called the "cradle of Indian temple architecture", and Pattadakal is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• There were three branches of the Chalukyas: the Badami (Vatapi) Chalukyas, the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi and the Western Chalukyas of Kalyani.

 

• Founders of other important dynasties: Rashtrakutas — Dantidurga; Pallavas — Simhavishnu (as a major power); Cholas (Imperial) — Vijayalaya; Palas — Gopala; Pratiharas — Nagabhata I; Sena — Samantasena.

 

NOTE

 

• Kirtivarman I (Option 1): The son of Pulakeshin I, who extended the kingdom and is called the first great ruler of the dynasty.

 

• Pulakeshin II (Option 2): The greatest Chalukya ruler, but not the founder of the dynasty.

 

• Vikramaditya VI (Option 4): A ruler of the Western Chalukyas of Kalyani, in whose court Bilhana wrote the *Vikramankadevacharita* and Vijnaneshwara wrote the *Mitakshara*.

question: The First Five Year Plan of India was based on which of the following economic models?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Harrod-Domar model.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The First Five Year Plan (1951-1956) was based on the Harrod-Domar model, developed independently by the economists Roy F. Harrod and Evsey Domar. (प्रथम पंचवर्षीय योजना — हैरोड-डोमर मॉडल)

 

• The model holds that the rate of growth of an economy depends on the level of saving and the capital-output ratio, and it therefore emphasises raising savings and investment as the key to growth.

 

• The plan gave priority to agriculture, irrigation and power, in view of the food shortage and the dislocation caused by Partition. Its target growth rate was 2.1%, and the achievement was 3.6% — making it, by that measure, the most successful of the plans.

 

• Major projects begun under it: the Bhakra Nangal, Hirakud, Damodar Valley and Mettur projects. Five Indian Institutes of Technology and the University Grants Commission (1956) also date from this period.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Models behind the other plans:
◦ Second Plan (1956-61) — the P.C. Mahalanobis model, stressing heavy and basic industries; also called the Nehru-Mahalanobis model. The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 was adopted in this plan.
◦ Third Plan (1961-66) — the Gadgil Yojana, aiming at a self-reliant and self-generating economy.
◦ Fourth Plan (1969-74) — growth with stability and progressive achievement of self-reliance, based on the Ashok Rudra and Alan S. Manne model.

 

• Planning in India began with the Planning Commission, set up by an executive resolution in 1950, with the Prime Minister as its Chairman. It was replaced by NITI Aayog on 1 January 2015.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahalanobis model (Option 1): The basis of the Second Five Year Plan, not the First.

 

• Gadgil model (Option 3): Associated with the Third Plan and later with the Gadgil Formula for the distribution of central assistance to states.

 

• Wage Goods model (Option 4): Proposed by C.N. Vakil and P.R. Brahmananda, it emphasised the production of wage goods, but it was not adopted for the First Plan.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the Iqta system of the Delhi Sultanate?

I. It was a system of assigning revenue from a piece of land to an officer in place of a cash salary.

II. It was systematically introduced in India by Iltutmish.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both statements are correct. (इक्ता व्यवस्था — इल्तुतमिश द्वारा प्रारंभ)

 

• Statement I is correct: under the Iqta system, the Sultan assigned the revenue of a territorial unit to an officer in lieu of a cash salary. The holder, called an Iqtadar or Muqti, collected the revenue, maintained a contingent of troops out of it, kept his own salary, and sent the surplus, called Fawazil, to the central treasury.

 

• Statement II is correct: although the institution was of West Asian origin, it was systematically introduced in India by Iltutmish (1211-1236), who divided his empire into Iqtas and assigned them to his Turkish nobles. It served both as a means of paying officers and as an instrument of administrative control.

 

• Important developments: Balban appointed a Khwaja to audit the accounts of the Iqtadars; Alauddin Khalji brought many Iqtas under direct central control; Firoz Shah Tughlaq made Iqtas hereditary, which weakened central authority.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Land was classified as Khalisa (crown land, whose revenue went directly to the Sultan), Iqta (assigned land) and Inam/Waqf (land granted to religious men and institutions).

 

• Other important terms of the Sultanate period: Kharaj (land tax), Jizya (a tax on non-Muslims), Zakat (a religious tax on Muslims), Khams (a share of war booty) and Diwan-i-Wizarat (the finance department).

 

• Tawarikh were the histories written in this period by scholars such as Ziauddin Barani (*Tarikh-i-Firozshahi*), Minhaj-us-Siraj (*Tabaqat-i-Nasiri*) and Amir Khusrau.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect, because both the given statements are factually accurate.

question: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 classified industries into how many categories or schedules?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Three.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 divided industries into three categories or schedules. (औद्योगिक नीति संकल्प 1956 — तीन श्रेणियाँ)

 

• The three schedules were:
◦ Schedule A — 17 industries whose future development was to be the exclusive responsibility of the State, including arms and ammunition, atomic energy, iron and steel, heavy machinery, coal, mineral oils, air transport and railways.
◦ Schedule B — 12 industries in which the State would progressively establish new undertakings, while private enterprise was expected to supplement State effort. These included machine tools, fertilisers, aluminium and other non-ferrous metals, and road and sea transport.
◦ Schedule C — all remaining industries, left to the private sector, though subject to the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951.

 

• The resolution is often called the "Economic Constitution of India" and gave effect to the goal of a "socialistic pattern of society" adopted at the Avadi Session of the Congress in 1955.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The number of industries reserved exclusively for the public sector was later reduced from 17 to 8 by the New Industrial Policy of 1991, then to 3 in 2001, and stands at 2 today — atomic energy and railway operations.

 

• The Industrial Policy Statement of 1977, announced by the Janata Government, emphasised small-scale, tiny and cottage industries, and defined a tiny unit as one with an investment of up to ₹1 lakh.

 

• The first Industrial Policy Resolution was that of 1948, presented by Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee, which established a mixed economy.

 

NOTE

 

• Two (Option 1), Four (Option 3) and Five (Option 4) are incorrect. The three-schedule classification of 1956 is the standard fact tested in examinations.

question: Which of the following rivers is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kosi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kosi is called the "Sorrow of Bihar" because of the devastating floods it causes and its habit of frequently shifting its course. (कोसी — बिहार का शोक)

 

• The river has shifted its channel westward by more than 100 km over the last two centuries, leaving behind a vast belt of sand and rendering large tracts unfit for cultivation. It carries an enormous load of silt from the Himalayas, which raises its bed and forces it out of its banks.

 

• The Kosi rises in Tibet and Nepal, is formed by the union of three streams — the Sun Kosi, Arun Kosi and Tamur Kosi, and is therefore also called the Saptakoshi. It is a left-bank tributary of the Ganga and joins it near Kursela in Bihar.

 

• The Kosi Project, undertaken jointly by India and Nepal, includes a barrage at Hanuman Nagar and embankments to control the flooding.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other rivers and their popular names:
◦ Damodar — the "Sorrow of Bengal", now largely controlled by the Damodar Valley Corporation (1948), India's first multipurpose river valley project, modelled on the Tennessee Valley Authority
◦ Godavari — the "Dakshin Ganga" and the longest river of peninsular India
◦ Brahmaputra — the "Sorrow of Assam"
◦ Krishna — sometimes called the "Vridha Ganga"
◦ Sabarmati and Sutlej — the Sutlej is known as the *Shatadru* in ancient texts

 

• Left-bank tributaries of the Ganga: Ramganga, Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak, Burhi Gandak, Kosi and Mahananda. Right-bank tributaries: Yamuna, Son, Punpun and Damodar.

 

NOTE

 

• Gandak (Option 1): A left-bank tributary rising in Nepal, where it is called the Narayani; it joins the Ganga at Hajipur.

 

• Son (Option 3): The most important right-bank tributary of the Ganga, rising from the Amarkantak plateau.

 

• Damodar (Option 4): Known as the "Sorrow of Bengal", not of Bihar.

question: A narrow strip of land that connects two larger landmasses is known as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is isthmus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An isthmus is a narrow strip of land that joins two larger landmasses and separates two bodies of water. (स्थलडमरूमध्य)

 

• Well-known examples:
◦ The Isthmus of Panama, joining North and South America, through which the Panama Canal was cut, linking the Atlantic and the Pacific.
◦ The Isthmus of Suez, joining Africa and Asia, through which the Suez Canal was cut, linking the Mediterranean and the Red Sea.
◦ The Isthmus of Kra in Thailand.

 

• The corresponding water feature is a strait — a narrow channel of water joining two larger water bodies and separating two landmasses. An isthmus and a strait are thus exact counterparts of each other.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other landforms frequently asked in SSC:
◦ Peninsula — land surrounded by water on three sides, as in the Indian peninsula
◦ Island — land surrounded by water on all sides
◦ Gulf — a large area of sea partly enclosed by land, larger than a bay
◦ Bay — a broad inlet of the sea where the land curves inward
◦ Cape — a pointed piece of land jutting into the sea
◦ Lagoon — a shallow body of water separated from the sea by a sandbar or reef, as Chilika in Odisha and Vembanad in Kerala
◦ Fjord — a long narrow inlet with steep sides, formed by glacial erosion

 

NOTE

 

• Strait (Option 1): A water channel, not land — for example the Palk Strait between India and Sri Lanka, the Strait of Malacca and the Bering Strait.

 

• Archipelago (Option 3): A group or chain of islands, such as the Andaman and Nicobar Islands or Indonesia.

 

• Delta (Option 4): A triangular deposit of silt formed at the mouth of a river, as the Sundarbans delta of the Ganga-Brahmaputra — the largest in the world.

question: Bile, which helps in the digestion of fats, is secreted by which organ of the human body?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Liver.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bile is secreted by the liver, the largest gland and the largest internal organ in the human body. It is then stored and concentrated in the gall bladder, from which it is released into the duodenum through the bile duct when food arrives. (पित्त — यकृत द्वारा स्रावित)

 

• Bile contains no digestive enzymes. It works in two ways:
◦ It emulsifies fats, breaking large globules into small droplets so that the enzyme lipase can act on them efficiently.
◦ It is alkaline, and so neutralises the acidic chyme arriving from the stomach, creating the medium in which pancreatic enzymes can work.

 

• The bile pigments are bilirubin and biliverdin, formed from the breakdown of haemoglobin. Excess bilirubin in the blood causes jaundice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other functions of the liver: storage of glycogen, detoxification of harmful substances including alcohol, synthesis of plasma proteins and urea, and storage of vitamins A, D and B12. The liver has a remarkable capacity for regeneration.

 

• The pancreas is a dual gland — as an exocrine gland it secretes pancreatic juice, containing trypsin, amylase and lipase; as an endocrine gland its islets of Langerhans secrete insulin and glucagon, which regulate blood sugar.

 

• The complete digestion of fat produces fatty acids and glycerol, which are absorbed by the lacteals of the intestinal villi and carried by the lymphatic system.

 

NOTE

 

• Pancreas (Option 1): Secretes pancreatic juice and hormones, but not bile.

 

• Gall bladder (Option 3): Stores bile; it does not produce it. Its removal does not stop bile secretion.

 

• Small intestine (Option 4): Secretes intestinal juice (succus entericus) and is the main site of digestion and absorption, but bile reaches it from the liver.

question: At which place did Gautama Buddha deliver his first sermon, in which he preached the Four Noble Truths?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sarnath.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gautama Buddha delivered his first sermon at Sarnath, near Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh, to his five former companions. This event is called the Dharmachakra Pravartana, or the "turning of the wheel of law". (सारनाथ — प्रथम उपदेश, धर्मचक्र प्रवर्तन)

 

• In this sermon he preached the Four Noble Truths (Arya Satya):
◦ Dukkha — the world is full of suffering
◦ Samudaya — suffering has a cause, namely desire
◦ Nirodha — suffering can be ended
◦ Magga — there is a path to end it, the Eightfold Path (Ashtangika Marga)

 

• The four principal events of the Buddha's life and their places:
◦ Birth — Lumbini (Nepal), symbolised by the lotus and bull
◦ Enlightenment (Nirvana) — Bodh Gaya, under a peepal tree on the bank of the Niranjana, symbolised by the Bodhi tree
◦ First sermon — Sarnath, symbolised by the wheel (Dharmachakra)
◦ Death (Mahaparinirvana) — Kushinagar, symbolised by the stupa

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath was adopted as the State Emblem of India on 26 January 1950, and the Dharmachakra from its abacus appears on the national flag.

 

• The Buddha was born in 563 BCE as Siddhartha, son of Suddhodana of the Shakya clan and Mahamaya. He attained enlightenment at the age of 35 and died at 80 in 483 BCE.

 

• Buddhist scriptures are the Tripitakas — Vinaya, Sutta and Abhidhamma Pitaka — written in Pali.

 

NOTE

 

• Bodh Gaya (Option 1): The place of his enlightenment, in Bihar; the Mahabodhi Temple there is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

 

• Kushinagar (Option 3): The place of his death or Mahaparinirvana, in Uttar Pradesh.

 

• Lumbini (Option 4): His birthplace, in Nepal; the site of the Rummindei Pillar of Ashoka.

question:
Which of the following subjects is/are included in the Union List of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution?

I. Defence of India

II. Police
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Only Statement I is correct. (संघ सूची — रक्षा; राज्य सूची — पुलिस)

 

• Statement I is correct: Defence of India is Entry 1 of the Union List, on which only Parliament can legislate.

 

• Statement II is incorrect: Police is Entry 2 of the State List, along with public order. Law and order is therefore primarily a responsibility of the State Governments.

 

• The Seventh Schedule divides legislative powers into three lists:
◦ Union List — originally 97 subjects, at present 100: defence, foreign affairs, atomic energy, railways, banking, currency, citizenship, post and telegraph.
◦ State List — originally 66 subjects, at present 61: police, public order, public health and sanitation, agriculture, prisons, local government, betting and gambling.
◦ Concurrent List — originally 47 subjects, at present 52: criminal law and procedure, marriage and divorce, education, forests, trade unions, electricity, economic and social planning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Education, forests, weights and measures, protection of wild animals and birds, and the administration of justice were transferred from the State List to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.

 

• In case of a conflict between a Union law and a State law on a Concurrent List subject, the Union law prevails (Article 254). Residuary powers — subjects not mentioned in any list — belong to Parliament under Article 248.

 

• The three-fold distribution was borrowed from the Government of India Act, 1935.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is incorrect because Defence is unquestionably a Union subject.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect because Police belongs to the State List, not the Union List.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect because Statement I is correct.

question: 'Ghumura' is a traditional folk dance of which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ghumura is a traditional folk dance of Odisha, associated particularly with the Kalahandi district. (घुमुरा — ओडिशा)

 

• It takes its name from the Ghumura, an earthen or wooden drum shaped like a pitcher, which the dancers hang from their necks and play while dancing. The dance is martial and heroic in character, and was traditionally performed before battle; it is now performed chiefly during the Nuakhai and Dussehra festivals.

 

• Other folk dances of Odisha: Chhau (Mayurbhanj), Danda Nata, Ranappa, Dalkhai, Karma Naach and Goti Pua. Odissi is the classical dance of the state and one of the eight classical dance forms of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Folk dances of the eastern and central states frequently asked in SSC:
◦ Jharkhand — Chhau, Paika, Jhumar, Karma
◦ West Bengal — Kathi, Gambhira, Baul, Chhau (Purulia)
◦ Assam — Bihu, Bagurumba, Jhumur
◦ Chhattisgarh — Panthi, Raut Nacha, Pandwani, Saila
◦ Bihar — Jat-Jatin, Bidesia, Jhijhian, Paika

 

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

 

NOTE

 

• West Bengal (Option 1): Known for Baul songs and the Purulia Chhau.

 

• Jharkhand (Option 2): Known for Chhau and Paika, both of which are also martial in character but distinct from Ghumura.

 

• Assam (Option 4): Known for Bihu, performed during the Bohag Bihu festival.

question: For most States and Union Territories of India, the reference date for the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 shall be ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1st March 2027.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The reference date for the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 shall be 00:00 hours of 1st March 2027 for all States and Union Territories, except Ladakh and the snow-bound areas of Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, for which it shall be 1st October 2026. (जनगणना 2027 — संदर्भ तिथि 1 मार्च 2027)

 

• The gazette notification for the census was issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs on 16 June 2025.

 

• Census 2027 will be conducted in two phases:
◦ Phase I — House Listing and Housing Census, to be carried out in 2026
◦ Phase II — Population Enumeration, to be carried out in 2027

 

• It will be the 16th Census of India and the 8th after Independence, the first since 2011. It will be India's first digital census, with a mobile application for enumerators and a self-enumeration facility, and it will also include the enumeration of castes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The census is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, in accordance with the Census Act, 1948.

 

• The first census in India was conducted in 1872 under Lord Mayo, and the first complete and synchronous census in 1881 under Lord Ripon, who is regarded as the Father of the Indian Census.

 

• Census 2011 recorded a population of 121.09 crore, a literacy rate of 74.04%, a sex ratio of 943 and a density of 382 persons per square kilometre.

 

NOTE

 

• 1st January 2027 (Option 1) and 1st April 2027 (Option 3) are not the notified reference dates.

 

• 1st October 2026 (Option 4) is the reference date only for Ladakh and the snow-bound areas of Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, where enumeration must be completed before the winter sets in.

question: The tribal festival 'Bhagoria', celebrated just before Holi, is associated with which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bhagoria is a colourful tribal festival celebrated chiefly by the Bhil and Bhilala communities of the Jhabua, Alirajpur, Dhar and Khargone districts of Madhya Pradesh. (भगोरिया — मध्य प्रदेश)

 

• It is held in the week preceding Holi, in the month of Phalgun, and coincides with the end of the harvest. Weekly markets (*haats*) turn into fairs where young men and women meet, and the festival is traditionally associated with the choosing of a life partner — a young man applies *gulal* to a girl, and if she returns it, the proposal is accepted.

 

• It was granted the status of a state festival by the Government of Madhya Pradesh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other festivals of Madhya Pradesh: Khajuraho Dance Festival, Tansen Samaroh (Gwalior), Lokrang Utsav (Bhopal), Malwa Utsav and the Nagaji Fair.

 

• Regional forms of Holi across India frequently asked in SSC:
◦ Lathmar Holi — Barsana and Nandgaon, Uttar Pradesh
◦ Baithki Holi and Khadi Holi — Kumaon, Uttarakhand
◦ Shigmo — Goa
◦ Yaosang — Manipur
◦ Hola Mohalla — Anandpur Sahib, Punjab, begun by Guru Gobind Singh
◦ Dol Jatra / Basanta Utsav — West Bengal
◦ Rang Panchami — Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh

 

NOTE

 

• Chhattisgarh (Option 2): Known for the Bastar Dussehra, the longest Dussehra celebration in the world, and the Madai festival.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 3): Known for the Pushkar Fair, Gangaur, Teej and the Desert Festival at Jaisalmer.

 

• Gujarat (Option 4): Known for Navratri, Uttarayan and the Rann Utsav.

question: The landing site of Chandrayaan-3 on the Moon, commemorated every year on National Space Day, has been officially named ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shiv Shakti Point.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The landing site of Chandrayaan-3 has been named "Shiv Shakti Point" (formally Statio Shiv Shakti). The name was announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 26 August 2023 and was approved by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in March 2024. (शिव शक्ति पॉइंट)

 

• Chandrayaan-3 made a successful soft landing near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023, making India the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon after the USSR, the United States and China, and the first to land near the south pole.

 

• 23 August is now observed every year as National Space Day. The lander was named Vikram and the rover Pragyan; the mission was launched by the LVM3-M4 rocket from Sriharikota. Its mission director was Mohana Kumar and the project director P. Veeramuthuvel, with S. Somanath as ISRO Chairman.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The site where the Chandrayaan-2 lander crash-landed in 2019 has been named "Tiranga Point".

 

• Chandrayaan-1, launched in 2008, was India's first lunar mission. Its Moon Impact Probe landed near the lunar south pole at a spot named Jawahar Point, and the mission confirmed the presence of water molecules on the Moon.

 

• Other recent ISRO milestones: Aditya-L1, India's first solar observatory, placed at the Lagrange point L1 in January 2024; Mangalyaan (2013), which made India the first country to reach Mars orbit in its first attempt; and the Gaganyaan human spaceflight programme.

 

NOTE

 

• Tiranga Point (Option 1): The Chandrayaan-2 impact site, not the Chandrayaan-3 landing site.

 

• Vikram Point (Option 3): Vikram is the name of the lander, not of the landing site.

 

• Jawahar Point (Option 4): The site where the Chandrayaan-1 Moon Impact Probe landed in 2008.

question: Why do we see a flash of lightning several seconds before we hear the sound of thunder?
option_1: Because light waves are longitudinal while sound waves are transverse
option_2: Because the speed of light is very much greater than the speed of sound
option_3: Because sound cannot travel through clouds at all
option_4: Because thunder is actually produced a few seconds after the lightning
solution_text:
The correct answer is Because the speed of light is very much greater than the speed of sound.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lightning and thunder are produced at the same instant, but we see the flash first because the speed of light is enormously greater than the speed of sound. (प्रकाश की चाल ध्वनि की चाल से बहुत अधिक)

 

• The figures make the difference clear:
◦ Speed of light in air ≈ 3 × 10⁸ m/s (3,00,000 km/s)
◦ Speed of sound in air ≈ 344 m/s at 22°C
◦ Light is therefore roughly 9,00,000 times faster than sound.

 

• For practical purposes the light reaches the observer instantaneously, while the sound takes about 3 seconds to travel 1 kilometre. Counting the seconds between the flash and the thunder and dividing by three gives the approximate distance of the storm in kilometres.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sound is a longitudinal mechanical wave that requires a material medium and cannot travel through a vacuum. Light is a transverse electromagnetic wave that travels fastest in a vacuum and needs no medium.

 

• The speed of sound is greatest in solids (about 5,960 m/s in steel), less in liquids (about 1,500 m/s in water) and least in gases. It increases with temperature, by roughly 0.6 m/s for every 1°C rise.

 

• The speed of light, by contrast, is greatest in a vacuum and decreases in a denser medium — about 2.25 × 10⁸ m/s in water.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 reverses the physics — sound waves are longitudinal and light waves are transverse, and in any case the difference in wave type is not the reason for the delay.

 

• Option 3 is wrong; sound travels perfectly well through air and clouds, only more slowly.

 

• Option 4 is wrong; thunder is produced by the rapid expansion of air heated by the lightning discharge, and so occurs at the same moment as the flash.

question: According to Census 2011, approximately what percentage of India's total population lived in rural areas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 68.8%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to Census 2011, about 68.84% of India's population lived in rural areas and 31.16% in urban areas. (जनगणना 2011 — ग्रामीण जनसंख्या लगभग 68.8%)

 

• In absolute terms this was roughly 83.3 crore people in rural India and 37.7 crore in urban India, out of a total population of 121.09 crore.

 

• The urban share had risen from 27.81% in 2001 to 31.16% in 2011. This was the first decade since Independence in which the absolute increase in urban population exceeded that in rural population.

 

• There were 640 districts, 5,924 sub-districts, 7,935 towns and about 6.4 lakh villages recorded in Census 2011.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other key Census 2011 figures: decadal growth 17.7%; density 382 persons per sq km; sex ratio 943; child sex ratio 919; literacy 74.04% (male 82.14%, female 65.46%).

 

• Himachal Pradesh is the least urbanised State (about 10% urban), while Tamil Nadu was the most urbanised major State (about 48.4%). Delhi (97.5%) is the most urbanised Union Territory.

 

• As per the sectoral composition of the workforce in 2011, about 54.6% of workers were engaged in the primary sector, though this sector contributes a far smaller share of Gross Value Added — an instance of disguised unemployment.

 

NOTE

 

• 58.8% (Option 1) understates the rural share considerably.

 

• 72.2% (Option 3) was approximately the rural share in Census 2001, when the urban share was 27.81%.

 

• 74.0% (Option 4) is close to the literacy rate of 2011 (74.04%) and is a common confusion in the examination hall.

question: 'BharatGen', launched in 2025, is India's first government-funded initiative of which of the following kinds?
option_1: A multimodal Large Language Model for Indian languages
solution_text:
The correct answer is A multimodal Large Language Model for Indian languages.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• BharatGen is India's first government-funded multimodal Large Language Model (LLM) initiative, launched in 2025 at the BharatGen Summit by the Union Minister of Science and Technology, Dr. Jitendra Singh. (भारतजेन — भारतीय भाषाओं के लिए बहुविध वृहद भाषा मॉडल)

 

• "Multimodal" means that it works across more than one form of data — it supports text, speech and image based outputs, and is being developed for the 22 scheduled Indian languages.

 

• It is led by the TIH Foundation for IoT and IoE at IIT Bombay and funded under the National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems (NM-ICPS) of the Department of Science and Technology. Partner institutions include IIT Bombay, IIIT Hyderabad, IIT Mandi, IIT Kanpur, IIT Madras and IIM Indore.

 

• Its distinguishing features are that it is multilingual and multimodal, trained on Indian datasets, and released as an open-source platform to build an ecosystem of generative AI research in the country. Its intended applications are in governance, health, education and agriculture.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Related national initiatives: the IndiaAI Mission, approved in 2024 to build computing capacity and datasets; Bhashini, the National Language Translation Mission for real-time translation across Indian languages; and the National Supercomputing Mission, under which the PARAM series of supercomputers is built.

 

• A Large Language Model is an AI system trained on very large volumes of text to understand and generate human language.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is incorrect — quantum research in India is pursued under the National Quantum Mission (2023).

 

• Option 3 is incorrect — the indigenous mobile operating system developed in India is BharOS, by IIT Madras.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect — India's digital payment infrastructure is the UPI, operated by the NPCI.

question: Which Indian state accounts for almost the entire production of lignite in the country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tamil Nadu accounts for the overwhelming share of India's lignite production, chiefly from the Neyveli field in the Cuddalore district. (नेवेली, तमिलनाडु — लिग्नाइट)

 

• Neyveli Lignite Corporation (NLC India Limited), established in 1956, mines the lignite and uses it to generate thermal power at pithead stations.

 

• Lignite is often called "brown coal". It is a low-grade coal with a high moisture content and a carbon content of about 40-55%, and it burns with a smoky flame. Because it crumbles easily and has low calorific value, it is generally used at the mine site itself rather than transported.

 

• The four types of coal in ascending order of quality are: Peat → Lignite → Bituminous → Anthracite. Anthracite is the highest grade, with over 80% carbon, and is found in India mainly in Jammu & Kashmir. Bituminous is the most widely used variety.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's coal reserves lie chiefly in the Gondwana formations, which supply about 98% of production; the Tertiary coalfields are found in Assam, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland.

 

• Major coalfields: Jharia, Bokaro, Giridih and Karanpura (Jharkhand); Raniganj (West Bengal); Korba (Chhattisgarh); Singrauli (Madhya Pradesh); Talcher (Odisha); Singareni (Telangana).

 

• The largest coal-producing state is Chhattisgarh, followed by Odisha and Jharkhand. India is the second largest producer and consumer of coal in the world after China.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajasthan (Option 2) and Gujarat (Option 3): Both have lignite deposits — at Barmer and Bikaner in Rajasthan and at Kutch and Bhavnagar in Gujarat — but their output is far smaller than that of Tamil Nadu.

 

• Jharkhand (Option 4): A leading producer of bituminous coal, not lignite; Jharia is famous for its coking coal reserves.

question: The headquarters of the New Development Bank, established by the BRICS nations, is located in which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shanghai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The New Development Bank (NDB), formerly called the BRICS Development Bank, has its headquarters at Shanghai, China. (न्यू डेवलपमेंट बैंक — शंघाई)

 

• It was established by an agreement signed at the Sixth BRICS Summit at Fortaleza, Brazil, in 2014, and began operations in 2015. Its purpose is to mobilise resources for infrastructure and sustainable development projects in the BRICS countries and other emerging economies.

 

• Its initial authorised capital was US$ 100 billion, with an initial subscribed capital of US$ 50 billion shared equally among the five founding members, so that each has an equal vote — a deliberate contrast with the weighted voting of the World Bank and IMF.

 

• Its first President was K.V. Kamath of India, and it has a regional centre in Africa at Johannesburg. Marcos Troyjo and later Dilma Rousseff of Brazil have also served as its President.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The term BRIC was coined by Jim O'Neill of Goldman Sachs in 2001. The grouping became BRICS when South Africa joined in 2010, attending its first summit at Sanya, China, in 2011.

 

• The first BRIC summit was held at Yekaterinburg, Russia, in 2009. From 2024, the grouping was expanded to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates.

 

• The BRICS also created the Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA), a currency-swap safety net of US$ 100 billion, at the same Fortaleza summit.

 

NOTE

 

• New Delhi (Option 2): India is a founding member and hosts BRICS summits, but not the bank's headquarters.

 

• Moscow (Option 3): Russia is a founding member; Moscow is not the seat of the NDB.

 

• Johannesburg (Option 4): The location of the NDB's Africa Regional Centre, but not of its headquarters.

question: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced in India through which Constitutional Amendment Act?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 101st Amendment Act.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced by the Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016, and came into force on 1 July 2017, observed as GST Day. (जीएसटी — 101वाँ संविधान संशोधन)

 

• GST is a destination-based, indirect tax levied on the supply of goods and services, and it subsumed a large number of earlier central and state taxes such as excise duty, service tax, VAT, octroi, entry tax and luxury tax.

 

• The amendment inserted Article 246A (concurrent power to tax), Article 269A (levy and collection of IGST on inter-state supply) and Article 279A (the GST Council).

 

• The GST Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister, with the Union Minister of State for Finance and the Finance Ministers of all States as members. Decisions require a three-fourths majority of weighted votes, in which the Centre has one-third and the States together two-thirds of the votes.

 

• GST has five main slabs — 0%, 5%, 12%, 18% and 28%. Its components are CGST, SGST/UTGST and IGST. Petroleum products, alcohol for human consumption and electricity remain outside its purview.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• GST was first recommended by the Kelkar Task Force (2003); the design was worked out by an Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers headed by Asim Dasgupta. France was the first country in the world to adopt GST, in 1954.

 

• Assam was the first state to ratify the GST Bill.

 

NOTE

 

• 99th Amendment Act (Option 1): Established the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC), later struck down by the Supreme Court in 2015.

 

• 100th Amendment Act (Option 2): Gave effect to the land boundary agreement with Bangladesh in 2015.

 

• 102nd Amendment Act (Option 4): Granted constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) in 2018.

question: In which of the following sports is a ball NOT used?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Badminton.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Badminton is played with a shuttlecock, not a ball. (बैडमिंटन — शटलकॉक)

 

• The shuttlecock, also called a shuttle or birdie, is an open conical projectile made of 16 feathers fixed in a cork base covered with leather; synthetic shuttles are also used. A standard feather shuttlecock weighs about 4.74 to 5.50 grams.

 

• Badminton is the only major racquet sport that does not use a ball; tennis, table tennis and squash all use balls.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Objects used in various sports, frequently asked in SSC:
◦ Badminton — shuttlecock
◦ Ice hockey — puck
◦ Archery — arrow
◦ Athletics (throws) — javelin, discus, shot, hammer
◦ Curling — stone
◦ Polo — ball and mallet
◦ Croquet — ball and mallet

 

• Badminton's governing body is the Badminton World Federation (BWF), headquartered at Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. The game developed at Pune in India, where it was called "Poona", before being taken to England.

 

NOTE

 

• Volleyball (Option 1): Played with a ball, by teams of six players; a set is played to 25 points.

 

• Water polo (Option 2): Played in a swimming pool with a ball, by teams of seven players including a goalkeeper.

 

• Handball (Option 4): Played with a ball, by teams of seven players.

question: Who is the author of the book 'The Argumentative Indian'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amartya Sen.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "The Argumentative Indian: Writings on Indian History, Culture and Identity" (2005) was written by Professor Amartya Sen. (द आर्गुमेंटेटिव इंडियन — अमर्त्य सेन)

 

• The book is a collection of essays arguing that India has a long and continuous tradition of public debate, heterodoxy and reasoned argument, and that this tradition is central to the success of Indian democracy and secularism.

 

• Amartya Sen was awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences in 1998 for his contributions to welfare economics and social choice theory, and the Bharat Ratna in 1999.

 

• His other works include "Poverty and Famines" (1981), "Development as Freedom" (1999), "The Idea of Justice" (2009), "An Uncertain Glory: India and its Contradictions" (with Jean Drèze) and "Home in the World", his memoir.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the game of Kabaddi?

I. Each team has seven players on the court at a time.

II. A raider must complete his raid within thirty seconds.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both statements are correct. (कबड्डी — 7 खिलाड़ी, 30 सेकंड की रेड)

 

• Statement I is correct: a Kabaddi team consists of 12 players, of whom 7 are on the court at any given time and 5 are substitutes.

 

• Statement II is correct: a raid must be completed within 30 seconds. The raider must cross into the opponents' half, touch one or more defenders and return to his own half while continuously chanting "kabaddi" — the cant — without taking a breath.

 

• Other rules worth remembering: a men's match consists of two halves of 20 minutes with a 5-minute interval; the court measures 13 m × 10 m for men and 12 m × 8 m for women. A "lona" or "lobh" of 2 bonus points is awarded when the entire opposing team is put out.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kabaddi is the state game of Tamil Nadu, and is known by different names in different regions — Hu-Tu-Tu in Maharashtra, Ha-Do-Do in eastern India, Chedugudu in Andhra Pradesh and Sadugudu in Tamil Nadu.

 

• It was introduced as a demonstration sport at the 1936 Berlin Olympics and became a regular medal event at the 1990 Beijing Asian Games. India has dominated the Kabaddi World Cup and the Asian Games in this discipline.

 

• The Pro Kabaddi League was launched in India in 2014 and has greatly popularised the sport.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect, because both the given statements accurately state the rules of the game.

question: The city of Kolkata grew around which fort built by the British East India Company?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fort William.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The city of Kolkata (Calcutta) developed around Fort William, built by the English East India Company on the eastern bank of the Hooghly river. (फोर्ट विलियम — कोलकाता)

 

• The original fort was begun in 1696 and named after King William III of England. It was captured by Siraj-ud-Daulah in 1756, the occasion of the notorious "Black Hole of Calcutta" episode. After the Battle of Plassey (1757), Robert Clive built a new and much stronger Fort William, completed in 1781, which stands today and houses the headquarters of the Eastern Command of the Indian Army.

 

• Job Charnock of the East India Company is traditionally regarded as the founder of Calcutta, which grew from the three villages of Sutanuti, Gobindapur and Kalikata.

 

• Fort William College was established there in 1800 by Lord Wellesley for the training of British civil servants in Indian languages, and it became an important centre of Bengali prose.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Presidency towns and their forts:
◦ Madras (Chennai) — Fort St. George, built in 1644, the first English fort in India
◦ Calcutta (Kolkata) — Fort William
◦ Bombay (Mumbai) — Bombay Castle; Bombay came to the English in 1661 as part of the dowry of Catherine of Braganza and was transferred by Charles II to the Company in 1668

 

• Calcutta was the capital of British India from 1772 to 1911, when the capital was shifted to Delhi by Lord Hardinge.

 

NOTE

 

• Fort St. David (Option 2): Located at Cuddalore in Tamil Nadu, purchased by the English in 1690.

 

• Fort St. George (Option 3): At Chennai, around which that city developed — the fort of Madras, not Calcutta.

 

• Fort Aguada (Option 4): A Portuguese fort in Goa, built in 1612.

question: The Trinity of Carnatic music consists of Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Syama Sastri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Trinity of Carnatic music comprises Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri. (कर्नाटक संगीत त्रिमूर्ति)

 

• All three were contemporaries who lived in the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries and were born at Tiruvarur in Tamil Nadu, and their compositions form the core of the Carnatic concert repertoire even today.
◦ Tyagaraja (1767-1847) — composed chiefly in Telugu; his Pancharatna Kritis are sung every year at the Thyagaraja Aradhana festival at Thiruvaiyaru.
◦ Muthuswami Dikshitar (1775-1835) — composed mainly in Sanskrit; known for his Navagraha Kritis and the Kamalamba Navavarna series.
◦ Syama Sastri (1762-1827) — the eldest of the three; composed largely in Telugu, chiefly in praise of the goddess Kamakshi, and was a master of complex rhythmic patterns.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Purandara Dasa (1484-1564) is regarded as the "Father of Carnatic Music" (Karnataka Sangeeta Pitamaha). He systematised the teaching of music, introducing the Sarali, Janti and Alankara exercises and the Mayamalavagowla raga as the first raga to be taught — a method still followed.

 

• The foundational treatise for both systems is the "Sangita Ratnakara" of Sharngadeva (13th century), the last work accepted as authoritative by both the Hindustani and Carnatic traditions. The 72 Melakarta scheme of ragas was set out by Venkatamakhin in the "Chaturdandi Prakashika".

 

• Principal instruments of Carnatic music: veena, mridangam, ghatam, kanjira, violin and nadaswaram.

 

NOTE

 

• Purandara Dasa (Option 1): The Father of Carnatic Music, but he lived nearly three centuries before the Trinity and is not one of them.

 

• Swathi Thirunal (Option 3): The Maharaja of Travancore and a prolific composer in both the Carnatic and Hindustani styles, but not a member of the Trinity.

 

• Annamacharya (Option 4): The great composer of Tirupati, regarded as the earliest known composer of Carnatic sankirtanas.

question: Who became the first Indian woman to fly a fighter aircraft solo?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Avani Chaturvedi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Flight Lieutenant Avani Chaturvedi became the first Indian woman to fly a fighter aircraft solo on 19 February 2018, when she flew a MiG-21 Bison from the Air Force Station at Jamnagar, Gujarat. The sortie lasted about 30 minutes. (अवनि चतुर्वेदी — लड़ाकू विमान की पहली भारतीय महिला एकल पायलट)

 

• She belongs to Rewa in Madhya Pradesh. Along with Bhawana Kanth and Mohana Singh, she was commissioned in June 2016 as part of the first batch of women fighter pilots of the Indian Air Force, after the fighter stream was opened to women on an experimental basis in 2015.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable Indian women achievers frequently asked in SSC:
◦ Radhika Menon — the first woman Captain in the Indian Merchant Navy, and the first woman to receive the IMO Award for Exceptional Bravery at Sea
◦ Harita Kaur Deol — the first Indian woman to fly solo in the IAF (in a transport aircraft, 1994)
◦ Punita Arora — the first woman Lieutenant General of the Indian Army and Vice Admiral of the Navy
◦ Kalpana Chawla — the first woman of Indian origin in space
◦ Bachendri Pal — the first Indian woman to climb Mount Everest (1984)
◦ Arunima Sinha — the first female amputee to climb Everest
◦ Aditi Pant — the first Indian woman to visit Antarctica

 

NOTE

 

• Bhawana Kanth (Option 2): Also of the first batch; she became qualified to undertake combat missions on a MiG-21 Bison in 2019 and took part in the Republic Day flypast in 2021.

 

• Mohana Singh (Option 3): The third member of the first batch; she became the first woman fighter pilot to fly the LCA Tejas.

 

• Shivangi Singh (Option 4): India's first woman Rafale fighter pilot, inducted into the Golden Arrows squadron.
